# Google's Gemini 4 Carbon Is Now Available: What It Does and Who Can Try It

> **In short:** Google announced that Gemini 4 Carbon is now available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. Google calls it its strongest model, built for harder, multi-step tasks. Everyday users can reach it through paid Google AI Ultra subscriptions in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.

If you have ever asked an AI tool a tough question and gotten a shallow answer, you know how much a stronger model can matter. Google has released a new top-tier model, and this article explains what it is, what it is built for, and where you might meet it.

## What Gemini 4 Carbon is

Gemini is Google's family of AI models. A model is the core engine that reads your request and writes a response, a bit like the engine in a car. Google places Gemini 4 Carbon at the top of its lineup, and describes it as its strongest model yet.

Google says Carbon is designed for work that tests the limits of a model's reasoning. That includes complex, multi-step coding and debugging, open-ended scientific research, and checking its own work over several rounds. Carbon sits alongside Gemini 4 Argon, which Google describes as the ideal choice for most software engineering and knowledge work. Carbon is for the harder jobs.

The trade-off is that Carbon uses more tokens than Argon. A token is a small chunk of text, roughly a word or part of one, that the AI reads and writes. More tokens means the model can spend more effort exploring a problem before it answers.

## Where you can try it

Google lists several ways to reach the model:

- **Developers and businesses**: Carbon is available through an API (a way for programs to talk to each other) in Google AI Studio and in Gemini for business, for paying developers and enterprises.
- **Google AI Ultra subscribers**: Google says Carbon is rolling out to all Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, in Google Antigravity (its tool for building software with AI), and in AI Mode in Search.
- **Pricing**: Costs can change, so check Google's official pricing page for current plan details before you commit to anything.

## A new feature for teams of agents

Google is also previewing a feature called /swarm in Google Antigravity. An agent is an AI that can carry out steps on its own, such as writing code, testing it, and fixing errors. With /swarm, one prompt can be split across a coordinated group of agents, and you can track their progress in real time. Google says Carbon can take the most demanding roles, such as architectural design, coordination, and auditing, while lighter, faster models handle parallel work.

Google has shared examples of what this approach produced, including an interactive 3D exhibition of the Eiffel Tower's construction and an open-world 3D game set on Google's Mountain View campus. These are Google's own demonstrations. Treat them as examples of what the company says is possible, not a promise about your own projects.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: If you have a paid Google AI Ultra subscription, you can use Carbon in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. Google's announcement focuses on hard, multi-step work, so try it on a question that has several parts.
- **For your business or work**: Google says Carbon is strong at reading dense files with charts and tables, and at producing spreadsheets, presentations, and reports. Test it on one real task from your work before you rely on it.
- **If you're just getting started**: You do not need to understand tokens or APIs to benefit. Start with a question you already know the answer to, so you can judge whether the response is accurate.
- **If you already use it**: If you have an Ultra subscription, give Carbon a messy, multi-step request, such as a draft plan you want checked one step at a time. Then compare its answer with the same question asked in a shorter form.

## Wrap-up

Gemini 4 Carbon is Google's newest top-tier model, aimed at difficult, multi-step work. Google says it is available to developers and businesses now, and to Ultra subscribers in several Google products. Whether it matters for you depends on what you ask AI to do. Today, open the Gemini app or AI Mode in Search and check whether Carbon appears for your account. Then pick one hard question from your week and see how it handles it.
